issues.description: Field Ride.abbreviation: The UML in the problem statement (problem_statement.md line 23) declares Ride.abbreviation as type char, but the solution implementation (src/de/tum/in/ase/Ride.java line 6) declares the field as String and the constructor/getter use String. This mismatch contradicts the UML and will confuse students about the expected type for the abbreviation attribute and its getter, and leads to inconsistent constructor signatures across the hierarchy.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the abbreviation attribute type consistent with the UML: change Ride.abbreviation to char in Ride.java, update the Ride constructor parameter to char and getAbbreviation() to return char, and update all subclasses and any constructor calls (RollerCoaster, LaunchedRollerCoaster, LaunchedDropdownTower) to accept and pass a char abbreviation.

issues.description: Constructor parameter mismatch between RollerCoaster and Ride: In the solution, RollerCoaster's constructor is declared as RollerCoaster(String name, char abbreviation, int numberOfLoopings) (src/de/tum/in/ase/RollerCoaster.java line 7) and calls super(name, abbreviation), but Ride's constructor in the solution is Ride(String name, String abbreviation) (src/de/tum/in/ase/Ride.java line 8). This type mismatch for the abbreviation parameter causes a compilation error and contradicts the UML requirement that subclass constructors accept superclass attributes in the same order and types (see problem_statement.md lines 5 and 23).
issues.suggestedFix: Align constructor parameter types across the inheritance hierarchy. Preferred fix (match UML): change Ride.abbreviation to char, update Ride's constructor and getAbbreviation(), and update RollerCoaster and its subclasses to accept a char abbreviation and pass it to super. Alternatively, if you choose String, change RollerCoaster and all subclasses to use String consistently. Ensure all constructors accept superclass attributes in the same order and types.

issues.description: The attribute/parameter 'abbreviation' represents the ride abbreviation. In the problem statement UML (Ride.abbreviation) it is declared as type 'char' (problem_statement.md lines 21-24). In the solution implementation, Ride.java declares the field as a String (solution_repository/src/de/tum/in/ase/Ride.java) and its constructor/getter use String, while RollerCoaster.java in the solution declares its constructor parameter 'abbreviation' as a char and calls super(name, abbreviation) (solution_repository/src/de/tum/in/ase/RollerCoaster.java). This yields a type mismatch between the conceptual specification (char) and the Ride implementation (String) and is likely to confuse students about the expected type and constructor signature (and would be a compile-time error if left inconsistent).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the type of 'abbreviation' consistent with the UML. Preferred fix: change Ride to use a primitive char for the abbreviation (private char abbreviation; constructor parameter char abbreviation; public char getAbbreviation()) and update all call sites (RollerCoaster constructor and any subclasses like LaunchedRollerCoaster/LaunchedDropdownTower) to use char parameters so signatures and super(...) calls match. Alternatively, if a String is intended, update the UML/problem statement to declare 'abbreviation: String' and adjust the RollerCoaster constructor to accept String as well.
